Plan for DRE-3698 — the switch goes both ways and every stand-down says what it did (re-plan, 2026-10-02).

This is the sixth epic of the wave DRE-3681. The first plan filed its eight cards on 2026-10-01 and was sent back on one defect only: the proof card had no real blocking relations behind its "blocked by" line and still wore a build role. This pass fixes that and tightens two cards. No card was added or removed.

What gets built, in plain terms:

Today, when the console moves the fleet off a capped Claude account by itself, it marks every repo as if an operator had moved it by hand. So the fleet never comes home when the account recovers, and the console then tells the operator to undo its own move. After this epic, a console-made move is marked as the console's, the fleet comes home by itself once the home account is healthy and under 80%, and the "running on a loaner account" reminder fires only when a person actually made the swap.

Second, every time the console decides not to move the fleet, the Subscriptions page says so. Today that happens for two reasons out of ten. Auto-switch being turned off, in particular, writes nothing at all. After this epic it writes one line, once an hour, saying the setting is off and where to turn it on.

Third, only the deployment that owns the fleet can Reconnect, switch the fleet, or advance the billing label. Any other console gets a plain refusal sentence before anything is spent. And one click is one switch: three submits inside ten seconds produce one move and one log line, not three.

The order:

1. Three cards start together: the placement fix (DRE-5495), the executor's stand-down lines (DRE-5496), and the loaner-reminder fix (DRE-5497). They touch different files.
2. Then the 80% recovery line (DRE-5498) and the owner gate (DRE-5499), each after the placement fix.
3. Then the pool's own stand-down lines (DRE-5500), after the executor's helper and the recovery line.
4. Then the one-click-one-switch debounce (DRE-5501), after the owner gate.
5. Last, the proof (DRE-5502), after all seven.

What changed since the first plan: the proof card now has a real blocking relation to each of the seven build cards, wears the operator role with the hand-built and no-code marks, and no build role. The placement card puts its end-to-end scenario in a new test file so it no longer shares a file with the executor card, which builds beside it. The owner-gate card no longer edits the writer-lease module, because the one-owner epic (DRE-3696) is rewriting that module under its own card.

What could go wrong: a repo could walk home too early if the 80% guard is misread, and the next tick would move it again. The pool and the executor could both write the same stand-down line, which a test forbids. The owner gate could refuse the real owner if the deployment's owner setting is wrong, and the refusal names that in a sentence. None of these cards touches a token or a secret; every one changes what the console records and refuses, so the worst case is a wrong line on the page, reversible by the next tick or a one-line fix.

Rough size: seven build cards, each one module and its tests, about one agent run each. The chain is serialized through three shared files, so expect about a day of wall-clock if the merges go straight through.

Proof: the operator reads the production switch log, the repos' placement reasons and the alert feed after the release, runs the refusal and the triple-submit on a local copy of the same release, and writes the readings into the repo with every time in Pacific. The CEO reads that record and closes the proof card himself; there is no demo sitting.

To start the build: move ONLY this epic to In Progress — the children promote automatically, in order. Do not move the children by hand.
